Harry Thaxter did well to finish 12th—our eighth man! Had either Coleman or Rutland been declared as a "B" team man, we should have taken another set of awards, but we must not be too greedy!
Bob Martin, Syd Roberts and Harry Thaxter even beat our eighth "A" team man. Altogether, we look back with profound satisfaction on this Championship Day.
Our third man, in 18th position, was Harry Thaxter. He completed the course in 9 hr. 11 min. 7 sec., and so gained a first-class standard medal.
Harry Thaxter and Charlie Speechley had a ding-dong battle down Lauriston Road for second place, Thaxter gaining the verdict by a very small margin.

The third place went to our "B" team, which, as far as the scoring went, consisted of "Juniors" Eddie Heather, Syd Roberts, Charlie Speechley and Harry Thaxter.
Harry Thaxter gave an excellent performance to finish fourth. Clayton's victory bears out the form which he has shown in open races this season.
Thus we retained the Berman Cup and, whilst we cheer the men who won it, we must not forget to add a word of congratulation to Harry Thaxter, who gained third prize in the handicap.
Churcher once again led the field home, and Harry Thaxter was successful in our handicap with an 8 min. allowance.
A gallant but unavailing effort by Harry Thaxter over the last mile reduced the margin to two points, but could not displace Surrey Walking Club, whose team rose to the occasion splendidly.
In the Metropolitan W.C. 15 mile Walk held in Regents Park, our team won the scratch race and also the handicap team event. Harry Thaxter won the individual handicap, with C.
Harry Thaxter won the individual handicap, with Charlie Churcher second; and so, inevitably, we won the handicap team race. The "Godstone," held on April 20th, did not find us quite so prominent.

Harry Thaxter, who showed such good form last season, unfortunately cracked up in the blitz and was invalided out of the Police. He is now back in the country recuperating and we wish him a speedy recovery.
Harry Thaxter, still at the Sun Inn, Diss, Norfolk, will be pleased to welcome any Belgravian visiting his district. It is understood that he has plenty of beer!
Harry Thaxter is not so busy in his pub. at Diss, Norfolk, now that the Americans have left, and hopes to pay us a visit. We are pleased to say that Harry is feeling much better.
Harry Thaxter is now an official of Diss Town F.C. and is on the committee of a tennis club. Jack Bidgood gave our Brighton walkers a cheery smile as they passed through his "beat."
The minutes of the last A.G.M. were read and signed. An apology for absence was read from H.
Harry Thaxter sends his best wishes to all his old friends, and will be pleased to see them at the Sun Hotel, Diss, at any time they are in the neighbourhood.
